name: Kneeling Cable Lat Pulldown
description: The kneeling lat pulldown is performed with the lifter kneeling on the floor in front of a high-pulley cable rather than seated in a machine. The kneeling position eliminates the ability to use the thigh pad for stabilization and increases core anti-extension demand. It trains the lat through a fuller overhead range of motion and allows the torso to shift freely, making it a useful variation for developing overhead pulling strength.

execution.starting_position: Attach a straight bar or rope to a high-pulley cable. Kneel on both knees directly below or slightly in front of the cable stack, hips over knees.
execution.setup_instructions: Position the knees hip-width apart. Set an appropriate weight for the kneeling position, which will typically be lighter than a seated pulldown.
steps: Step 1: Kneel facing the cable stack with arms extended overhead gripping the attachment.
Step 2: Brace the core and maintain a neutral spine throughout.
Step 3: Initiate by depressing the scapulae and pulling the elbows down toward the floor.
Step 4: Pull until the bar or hands reach chin or upper chest level.
Step 5: Return under control to full overhead extension without losing spinal alignment.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return to the overhead position.
common_mistakes: Allowing the lower back to hyperextend as the cable pulls the torso forward
Using momentum by rocking the hips
Not fully extending the arms at the top
safety_considerations: Keep the core braced throughout to protect the lumbar spine under the overhead cable pull
Use a lighter weight than your seated pulldown to account for reduced stability
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Arms fully extended overhead at the start, pulled to upper chest or chin level at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Don't let the cable pull you forward
Squeeze the lats hard at the bottom
